pages.label: LESSON 1 / START HERE
pages.title: My AI Starting Plan
pages.intro: Choose a small, useful task. You do not need to understand every AI feature to begin. Keep this toolkit and write on the printed pages; nothing is submitted online.
pages.activity: Choose three everyday tasks AI might help with. Circle one to try and identify the personal details you can leave out.

blocks.heading: TRY SOMETHING USEFUL
blocks.text: Ideas: plan a simple meal, draft a thank-you note, explain a hobby, or make a packing list.

blocks.field: Three everyday tasks I would like help with
The first task I will try

blocks.heading: BUILD A SAFETY HABIT
blocks.text: Use made-up names or general descriptions. Leave out passwords, identity numbers, banking details, and private family information. AI can be mistaken even when it sounds confident.

blocks.field: Details I can leave out or replace

blocks.check: I can explain one useful thing AI can do and one reason to check its answer.

pages.label: LESSON 2 / ASK CLEARLY
pages.title: My Everyday Prompt Cards
pages.intro: A prompt is the request you give an AI. Start with one example below, then change the words to fit your life. Do not add sensitive personal information.
pages.activity: Try one prompt, ask for an improvement, and save the version that helps you. Use fictional details during the group demonstration.

blocks.heading: 1 / HELP ME WRITE
blocks.text: Help me draft a short thank-you note to a neighbor who watered my plants. Make it warm and natural. Leave out names and addresses.

blocks.heading: 2 / HELP ME UNDERSTAND
blocks.text: Explain how a home Wi-Fi router works in plain language. Use one everyday example. Ask me if I would like a simpler explanation.

blocks.heading: 3 / HELP ME PLAN
blocks.text: Make a packing checklist for a two-day trip in rainy weather. Group it into clothing, essentials, and optional items.
Improve any answer: Make it shorter. Give me another example. What should I double-check?

blocks.check: I removed private details and read the result before using or sharing it.

pages.label: LESSON 3 / PROTECT YOUR FAMILY
pages.title: My Family Safety Plan
pages.intro: A familiar voice can be imitated. Agree privately on a family safe word or phrase before an emergency. Do not write the actual word on this worksheet or enter it into an AI tool.
pages.activity: Practice responding to an urgent family call using a pretend code word. Later, agree on your real family phrase privately and complete your trusted callback contacts.

blocks.heading: PAUSE. ASK. CALL BACK.
items: Pause before acting on an urgent request.
Ask the caller for the family phrase. Do not say it first or offer hints.
Hang up and dial a number you already trust. Do not use a new number supplied by the caller.

blocks.text: Even a correct phrase is only one check. Verify independently before sending money or private information. If the person cannot give it, do not assume they are safe or in danger; use your callback plan.

blocks.heading: AGREE PRIVATELY
blocks.text: Choose something memorable that is not a birthday, pet name, or public fact. Share it only with trusted family members. Replace it if it becomes known to others.

blocks.field: Trusted contact 1 / name and known phone number
Trusted contact 2 / name and known phone number

blocks.check: We chose our family phrase privately and practiced calling back.

blocks.text: Cannot reach the person? Contact another trusted person. If you believe there is immediate danger, call your local emergency number. In the U.S., call 911.

blocks.note: Based on FTC family emergency scam guidance and FBI identity-verification guidance. Source links are on page 7 of the complete toolkit.

pages.label: LESSON 4 / CHECK THE ANSWER
pages.title: My Answer-Checking Worksheet
pages.intro: Use AI to get started, then check the part that matters. Practice with something low stakes, such as a museum's opening hours or a gardening question.
pages.activity: Ask an everyday question, pick one claim from the answer, and verify it on an appropriate original source. Record anything you could not confirm.

blocks.field: One claim AI made that I need to check

blocks.heading: CHECK THE ORIGINAL SOURCE
blocks.text: Open the actual page, not just the AI's summary. Check who published it, when it was updated, and whether it supports the claim. A link by itself does not prove the answer is right.

blocks.field: Source title or website / date checked
What I confirmed, corrected, or still do not know

blocks.check: I will not act on an important claim that I could not verify.

blocks.text: For decisions about your health, money, or legal situation, involve a qualified professional. AI can help prepare questions; it should not make those decisions for you.

pages.label: LESSON 5 / KEEP PRACTICING
pages.title: My Seven-Day Practice Plan
pages.intro: Spend about 10 minutes at a time. You can repeat a day or go more slowly. Each activity pairs a useful skill with a safety habit.
pages.activity: Choose a realistic practice schedule. Finish with one useful result, explain how you checked it, and identify the precaution you used.

blocks.check: Day 1: Pick an everyday task. Remove details the AI does not need.
Day 2: Try a prompt card. Read the answer before using it.
Day 3: Ask for a clearer answer. Check one factual claim.
Day 4: Make your family callback plan. Agree on the code word privately.
Day 5: Practice an urgent-call scenario. Use a pretend phrase.
Day 6: Create a useful note, checklist, or plan. Correct any mistakes.
Day 7: Show a trusted person your result and explain one safety precaution.

blocks.field: What I checked and the precaution I took
Someone I can ask for help

pages.label: KEEP NEAR YOUR PHONE
pages.title: Pause. Ask. Call back.
pages.intro: An urgent call sounds like someone you love. Take a breath. You can care about them and still check who is calling.

blocks.heading: 1 / PAUSE
blocks.text: Do not rush to send money or reveal private information. A familiar voice or caller ID is not proof of identity.

blocks.heading: 2 / ASK
blocks.text: Ask for your family's private code word or phrase. Let the caller provide it. Do not reveal it or offer clues.

blocks.heading: 3 / CALL BACK
blocks.text: End the call. Dial your loved one's saved, trusted number. Even a correct code word does not replace this check.

blocks.heading: IF YOU STILL CANNOT CONFIRM
blocks.text: Contact another trusted person. Do not send money while you are unsure. If you believe there is immediate danger, call your local emergency number; in the U.S., call 911.
Keep the actual code word OFF this card. Never enter it into an AI tool or a public form.

blocks.note: Family safety guidance: FTC and FBI. See source links on page 7 of the complete toolkit, available at lifequestai.com/workshop/handouts.html.

pages.label: FOR FAMILIES AND FACILITATORS
pages.title: Practice Together
pages.intro: The goal is a useful result and a habit of checking. Read instructions aloud, allow extra time, and offer help without taking over.

blocks.heading: A FIVE-MINUTE FAMILY CALL PRACTICE
items: Agree that this is a pretend scenario. Never use a real emergency or your real family phrase in a group.
One person plays a caller asking for urgent money. The other practices pausing, asking for the phrase, and ending the call.
Practice finding a saved contact and explaining how you would call back. Do not place calls to emergency services during practice.
Discuss what felt difficult and how a trusted person could help.

blocks.heading: FINISH WITH SOMETHING USEFUL
blocks.text: Each participant shows a note, checklist, explanation, or plan they made with AI. Ask: What did you change? What did you check? What private information did you leave out?

blocks.heading: PRINTING AND PRIVACY
blocks.text: Print on U.S. Letter paper at Actual Size, or use Fit for A4. Single-sided printing leaves room for notes. Keep completed contact sheets private. The website does not collect worksheet answers or family code words.

blocks.heading: SOURCES FOR FAMILY SAFETY
blocks.text: FTC: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money. Explains voice impersonation and independently contacting family.
FBI: Identity-verification recommendations, including a private family word or phrase (December 19, 2025).
